## Statement · **draft**
Let $p$ be a prime and $G$ a finite group. If $|G| = p^{n}$ with $n \ge 0$, then $G$ is a **$p$-group**.

Equivalently, every element of $G$ has order a power of $p$: the order of an element divides $|G|$, hence can only be a power of $p$; conversely, if every element has order a power of $p$, then by Cauchy's theorem $|G|$ has no other prime divisor, so $|G|$ is a power of $p$.
